text.arabic_uthmani: لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِٱللَّغْوِ فِىٓ أَيْمَٰنِكُمْ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا عَقَّدتُّمُ ٱلْأَيْمَٰنَ ۖ فَكَفَّٰرَتُهُۥٓ إِطْعَامُ عَشَرَةِ مَسَٰكِينَ مِنْ أَوْسَطِ مَا تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ أَوْ كِسْوَتُهُمْ أَوْ تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍۢ ۖ فَمَن لَّمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍۢ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ كَفَّٰرَةُ أَيْمَٰنِكُمْ إِذَا حَلَفْتُمْ ۚ وَٱحْفَظُوٓا۟ أَيْمَٰنَكُمْ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ

baseline.text: Allah, düşünmeden ettiğiniz yeminlerden dolayı sizi sorumlu tutmaz; fakat bile bile bağladığınız yeminlerden dolayı sorumlu tutar. Bunun karşılığı, ailenize yedirdiğinizin orta ölçüsünden on yoksulu doyurmak, onları giydirmek veya bir köleyi özgür bırakmaktır. Bunları bulamayan üç gün oruç tutmalıdır. Yemin ettiğinizde yeminlerinizin karşılığı budur. Yeminlerinizi koruyun. Allah ayetlerini size böyle açıklar ki şükredesiniz.

findings.text: Yalnız bilerek düğümlenmiş yemin sözü sorumluluk doğurur; amaçsız söz böyle bir bağ kurmaz.
Kefaret, bozulan söz bağını yoksulu doyurma, giydirme, özgürleştirme veya oruç yoluyla toplumsal karşılığa çevirir.
Yeminleri korumak, söz ile eylem arasında açık ve yürünebilir bir yol bırakır.

activation_trace.role: Accountability for what issued from a person supplies the legal grasp applied on both sides of the contrast.
The image of something discarded and not counted supplies the no-liability threshold.
Binding and ratifying an undertaking makes deliberate oath-speech an enforceable bond.
The oath and sworn undertaking image identifies the repeated object being formed, repaired, and guarded.

changed_reading.after: Only speech deliberately consolidated into an oath-bond enters accountability; uncounted verbal overflow does not.
changed_reading.before: All oath-like speech appears to create one undifferentiated liability.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The repeated accountability verb contrasts "باللغو" with "بما عقدتم الأيمان".
baseline_models.mechanism: Speech enters liability only when it is intentionally tied into a durable oath-bond. Laghw is thrown out of the account, while عقد makes the oath something graspable as a commitment.

activation_trace.role: Tying endpoints supplies the binding condition that the remedy must answer.
Covering the wrong until its operative trace is removed supplies the reparative function of expiation.
Feeding another, especially one in need, turns private speech-liability into transferred sustenance.
A middle rank between high and low calibrates the transfer to an ordinary domestic standard.
The household circle supplies the familiar care-standard exported to people outside it.
Freedom opposed to bondage makes release a direct counter-movement to the oath's binding.
Means and material sufficiency gate the outward options without erasing responsibility.
Fasting as restraint relocates repair into the body when outward means are unavailable.

changed_reading.after: It designs a capacity-sensitive de-binding process that translates speech into measured care, liberation, or self-restraint.
changed_reading.before: The verse lists interchangeable penalties for a broken oath.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The oath-knot is followed by expiation through feeding, clothing, freeing a neck, or, when means fail, fasting.
baseline_models.mechanism: The remedy does not privately cancel the bond. It converts a verbal liability into outward provision measured by ordinary household care, or into human release; lack of means converts it into embodied restraint.

activation_trace.role: The right hand and rightward side give the oath an embodied image of exercised agency.
Power, capacity, and the side of right make oath-keeping stewardship of consequential speech.
Guarding and tending an entrusted thing supplies ongoing custody rather than a single act of compliance.
Covenant and persistent alliance extend the oath from utterance into a maintained relation.

changed_reading.after: It also calls for custody of the power by which binding commitments are made, including disciplined repair when that power is mishandled.
changed_reading.before: "Guard your oaths" means only never to break a sworn statement.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The repeated أيمان is finally governed by "واحفظوا أيمانكم".
baseline_models.mechanism: The oath sense remains primary, but the right-hand, force, and custody branches overlay it with agency. What is guarded is not only each promise's duration but the human capacity to bind oneself and others through authorized speech.

activation_trace.role: The focus supplies the tied knot whose force needs lawful management.
Prohibition as active prevention supplies the danger of turning voluntary speech into a self-made ban.
The image of untying a knot directly reverses the focus's image of binding one.
Expiatory covering supplies the authorized transition out of the self-made bond.

changed_reading.after: It can function as a boundary-preserving release that prevents deliberate human vows from manufacturing permanent prohibitions while retaining accountability for deliberate speech.
changed_reading.before: Expiation is simply a payment after violating any vow.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding prohibition on forbidding good things and the branch image of untying a knot recast expiation as a lawful release valve: a human oath-knot must not harden into a rival prohibition on what God has opened.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the sequence and the عقد knot versus حل untying images; I infer an arrow from self-binding over lawful goods to authorized release. A live alternative is that 5:87-88 and 5:89 regulate adjacent but independent conduct.
structural_cues: 5:87 says not to prohibit the good things God made lawful, and 5:88 commands eating lawful good provision immediately before the oath rule.
The focus offers food-related repair rather than allowing a verbal restriction to become permanent.

activation_trace.role: A middle rank supplies a stable measure instead of volatile or maximal extraction.
Feeding the needy directs the cost toward sustenance rather than reciprocal contest.
Gambling and division by lots supply the nearby rival mechanism of uncertain value transfer.
Enmity supplies the social output of the rival mechanism that measured repair avoids.

changed_reading.after: It is a measured, non-chance conversion of private liability into sustenance, with a social form opposite to rivalrous extraction.
changed_reading.before: The ten-person household-standard remedy is an arbitrary tariff.

context_deltas.mechanism: The fixed quantity, household midpoint, and needy recipients of oath repair contrast with gambling's chance allocation and its production of rivalry. The remedy redirects value through a predictable, relational measure rather than adversarial gain.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a measured support transfer in 5:89 and chance allocation producing hostility in 5:90-91; I infer that the former repairs social relations by opposing the latter's mechanics. The alternative is that their adjacency is thematic rather than contrastive.
structural_cues: The gambling prohibition follows the oath rule immediately.
5:91 explicitly links gambling to enmity, hatred, and blockage of remembrance and prayer.

activation_trace.role: The uncounted image supplies the focus's lower intent threshold.
A settled heart or resolve supplies the focus's positive intent threshold.
Deliberate aim confirms that the parallel liability also turns on intention.
Equivalence and balancing supply proportional calibration to the parallel repair.
The same expiatory covering marks the hunting response as a second instance of the repair architecture.
Feeding others repeats outward sustenance as a reparative channel.
Materially constrained recipients repeat the social destination of repair.
Fasting repeats embodied restraint as the convertible alternative.
Leaving punishment and effacing fault supplies the treatment of what preceded the rule.
Return after departure supplies the repeat-offense boundary beyond ordinary repair.

changed_reading.after: Its menu is one realization of a broader intent-sensitive, proportional, capacity-aware repair calculus.
changed_reading.before: 5:89 contains a one-off menu peculiar to oath breach.

context_deltas.mechanism: The hunting rule reuses expiation, feeding the poor, and fasting, while adding deliberateness, equivalence, pardon of what has passed, and a boundary at repetition. This exposes a portable repair calculus: intent activates liability, proportional outward action answers it, capacity selects the mode, and return changes the status.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated remedy template and its added modifiers; I infer a shared legal architecture across oath and hunting violations. The live alternative is that equivalence, adjudication, and recurrence are domain-specific additions rather than general features of oath expiation.
structural_cues: 5:95 exactly repeats the sequence expiation, food for poor people, or fasting.
The parallel rule adds deliberate action, judged equivalence, pardon of the past, and a consequence for returning.

activation_trace.role: Covering supplies the potentially ambiguous image that context must distinguish from hiding.
Manifestation and disclosure keep the repaired matter intelligible rather than suppressed.
Emergence into view supplies one pole of the explicit disclose-conceal contrast.
Hiding and covering up supply the rejected alternative to reparative covering.

changed_reading.after: It covers liability through inspectable repair, not through suppressing the breach or its truth.
changed_reading.before: Expiation covers a fault by making it disappear from view.

context_deltas.mechanism: The nearby opposition between what is made manifest and what is concealed separates expiatory covering from secrecy. Kaffara covers the operative trace of fault by an outward repair, while the verse's closing clarification keeps the truth legible.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two different covering mechanisms, one reparative and one concealing; I infer that visible performance distinguishes them. The alternative is that the disclose-conceal pair addresses divine knowledge without commenting on expiation.
structural_cues: The focus's remedies are observable acts of feeding, clothing, release, or fasting.
5:99 pairs what people disclose with what they conceal, and 5:106 later calls concealment of testimony sinful.

activation_trace.role: The sworn undertaking supplies the focus object later deployed in a public procedure.
Preserving covenant and protected trust becomes custody of the oath's public reliability.
Making meaning clear by speech or sign links guarded oaths to truthful evidence.
Testimony as knowledgeable declaration supplies the public truth-task assigned to sworn speech.
An oath formally apportioned to its bearers supplies the procedural act used to secure testimony.
Rejecting what proves false supplies correction rather than blind preservation of prior sworn claims.
The explicit sequence of oaths after earlier oaths shows that sworn evidence can be procedurally superseded.

changed_reading.after: It preserves the credibility of binding speech, which includes exposing false use and allowing truth-governed procedural reversal.
changed_reading.before: Guarding oaths preserves a private bond at all costs.

context_deltas.mechanism: The witness procedure uses sworn speech as public evidence and permits later oaths to displace earlier ones when wrongdoing is discovered. Guarding oaths therefore protects evidentiary reliability, not the immutability of every sworn claim.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies oath-backed testimony and a correction mechanism; I infer that preserving oaths means preserving their truth-bearing institution. A live alternative is that the witness procedure is a special forensic use with no broader effect on 5:89.
structural_cues: 5:106-108 moves from witnesses swearing, through discovery of culpability, to replacement witnesses and oaths after prior oaths.
The stated aim is testimony delivered "on its face," with fear that prior oaths may be returned.

activation_trace.role: Feeding others supplies the material act whose meaning context expands beyond transfer of calories.
A manifest sign connects the repaired act to the focus's closing disclosure.
Recognizing and displaying benefit supplies the intended response to the repaired provision.
A table bearing food supplies the concrete setting in which eating becomes evidence.
Stillness and assurance supply the inward effect sought through shared eating.
Fulfilled word and verified deed make food a test of whether speech has become true in action.
The table explicitly becomes a visible sign, linking provision to intelligible confirmation.
Apportioned gift and provision supply the table's outward beneficence.

changed_reading.after: Feeding can also be a credibility-restoring sign: a word's repair becomes tangible as provision received by others.
changed_reading.before: Feeding is merely the monetary equivalent of an oath penalty.

context_deltas.mechanism: The table sequence links eating with heart-assurance, verified truth, witness, sign, and provision. By analogy, feeding in expiation can make repaired credibility materially perceptible: provision becomes a social sign that a failed word has been answered.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the food-to-assurance-to-truth-to-sign sequence; I infer an analogical arrow from expiatory feeding to restored credibility. The materially live alternative is that the miraculous table confirms revelation and does not characterize ordinary expiatory meals.
structural_cues: 5:112-114 moves in sequence from a requested table, to eating and heart-assurance, to truth, witness, sign, and provision.
The focus itself moves from feeding to clarified signs and gratitude.

activation_trace.role: The oath as a sworn undertaking supplies the form of truth-bearing speech under custody.
Persistent maintenance carries the oath's truth-value beyond the instant of utterance.
Benefit opposed to harm supplies the final yield assigned to truth.
Truthful saying names the durable quality that ultimately proves beneficial.
Ultimate sovereignty places every human act of binding speech beneath God's final jurisdiction.

changed_reading.after: It restores a person's speech to a truth-bearing economy whose value persists to final judgment under divine sovereignty.
changed_reading.before: Oath repair settles a short-term private breach.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing judgment says that truth itself benefits the truthful, then locates all dominion with God. This extends guarded oath-speech across time: expiation repairs failure, but the enduring value being protected is truthful speech under final ownership and audit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies final benefit for truth and universal divine sovereignty; I infer that oath-custody preserves speech for that terminal audit. The alternative is that 5:119 concerns truth generally without a special return to oaths.
structural_cues: 5:119 explicitly makes the truth of truthful people beneficial on the final day.
5:120 closes the packet with God's sovereignty over everything.

remaining_uncertainties: The adjacency of 5:87-88 may frame oath-driven self-denial specifically, or it may only place independent rules beside one another.
The table-sign analogy is productive but may not define ordinary expiatory feeding.
The right-hand capacity overlay and the covering-clothing echo should remain qualified branch activations rather than lexical disambiguations.
strongest_changes: The 5:87-89 sequence and the عقد versus حل branch reversal recast expiation as an authorized release from self-made prohibition.
The exact remedy recurrence in 5:95 exposes an intent-sensitive, proportional, capacity-aware repair architecture.
The oath-backed witness procedure in 5:106-108 turns guarding oaths into protection of public evidentiary reliability.
The table sequence in 5:112-114 makes feeding legible as a possible material sign of restored credibility.
summary.what_was_special: The packet repeatedly moved the focus from private vow management into boundary calibration, restorative provision, public evidence, and durable truth. The strongest activation was the collision between the focus's oath-knot and the preceding root image of lawful untying.

activation_trace.role: Covering and overlaying supply the abstract image of expiation.
Garment and clothing perform the covering image as a concrete benefit to another person.

changed_reading.after: Clothing may also stage the semantic image of expiation: moral covering becomes a literal, beneficial covering of another.
changed_reading.before: Clothing is simply one fungible item in the remedy list.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it reads one remedy as materially enacting a root image of the remedy's name. It remains anchored in the focus's كفارة and كسوتهم, but should be rendered only as a lexical-material echo, not as etymological proof or a claim that clothing is the privileged option.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The covering image in كفارة stands beside the option of literally clothing the recipients.

activation_trace.role: Tying endpoints supplies the bond created by deliberate speech.
Freedom opposed to slavery supplies the exact counter-movement to binding.
The human neck supplies the person whose imposed bond is removed.
Servitude as ownership sharpens the human bond reversed by liberation.
Possession and disposal locate human release within the packet's closing claim about true ownership.

changed_reading.after: It can be read as a deliberate counter-bond: repair for self-binding speech takes the form of removing an imposed bond from another human.
changed_reading.before: Freeing a neck is merely a high-value substitute in a penalty schedule.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a cross-domain reversal from verbal bond to human bondage. It remains validly anchored in عقدتم and تحرير رقبة and is sharpened by the packet's later servant and dominion language; downstream prose should call it an anti-isomorphic structural analogy, not an exclusive rationale or an equation of oath and enslavement.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: A self-made oath-knot can be answered by the option that frees a human neck.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Only deliberately knotted speech bears liability.** `ل غ و B001` is what is set aside as not counting, `ع ق د B001` fastening a knot, and `ي م ن B003` oath by the right hand. I infer that legal force arises when speech is intentionally tied into obligation, distinguishing noise from binding utterance.
2. **Expiation converts a broken verbal bond into social provision.** `ط ع م B002` is feeding, `و س ط B001` just middle quality, `ك س و B001` garment-cover, `ح ر ر B002` freedom, and `ر ق ب B004` the enslaved person. I infer that repair redirects failed speech into food, covering, or released agency; inability turns to `ص و م B001`, embodied withholding.
3. **Guarding oaths keeps a clear road.** `ح ف ظ B003` is steady observance and `B007` a clear unbroken road. I infer that careful speech prevents repeated knots and repairs from obstructing communal trust.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later ayah 5:120 made the fixed ayah's local distinctions newly visible as bounded operations within a single encompassing dominion, rather than as an isolated rule or episode.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Only speech made into a knot creates the repair burden.** Fixed **ل غ و / B001** (“the thing set aside as not counting”) excludes unbound utterance, while fixed **ع ق د / B001** (“fastening ends into a knot”) and **B002** (“binding and ratifying an obligation”) identify the accountable oath. The repair then converts a private verbal bond into food, clothing, liberation, or disciplined time; 5:87–5:88 have just restored lawful goods to use. I infer that expiation unties a failed self-binding by releasing value toward vulnerable bodies or constraining the oath-maker’s body. The ayah reads oath law as material repair of consequential speech.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 5:90’s entangling practices supplied a negative image of binding, and 5:93’s repeated guarding showed the sustained discipline needed after consequential speech and consumption.

words.gloss_range: opening legal negation that excludes liability only for the stated idle-oath ground
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) opens by blocking divine account-taking for one oath category. The negation is scoped: it removes liability for idle oath material before the verse turns to deliberate binding, so mercy and accountability are sorted before the remedy appears.

topics.headline: legal negation opens the exemption side
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah first removes false liability before building the expiation rule.
topics.reason: The negative particle governs the first accountability verb and the later adversative clause supplies the contrasting liable case.

words.gloss_range: Form III holding-to-account directed at the addressed community, here negated for idle material inside oaths
words.prose: {{ar:يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ}} ({{tr:yuʾākhidhukumu}}) names divine holding-to-account with the pressure of being taken into consequence, but the opening negation withholds that grasp for idle oath speech. The same verb returns after the pivot, so liability changes by ground, not by a different divine action. Variant easing of the medial hamza changes the articulation without changing the juridical force.
words.root_gloss_range: taking, seizing, receiving, adopting, and holding to account; the local Form III use selects legal accountability while retaining seizure pressure

topics.headline: accountability verb is negated for idle oath speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels accountability as a named grasp that is withheld only for idle oath material.
topics.reason: The Form III verb with object suffix selects legal accountability; taking and seizure imagery survives as pressure, while the causal phrase limits the negation to idle oath material.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name as explicit agent of the opening accountability clause
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:allāhu}}) is the explicit subject of the opening rule. The divine name anchors both non-seizure for idle oath speech and seizure for deliberate binding, while broader derivational pressure around worship and refuge stays secondary to the local role of legal agency. The oath-law doublet (2:225) keeps that same divine standard across passages, and the gratitude close in the purity-law passage (5:6) shows the same divine intention operating in another legal setting.
words.root_gloss_range: divinity, worship, refuge, and awe; here the proper name functions as the named divine agent of accountability and clarification

topics.headline: same divine agent releases and binds
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees exemption and liability as one divine legal standard rather than two authorities.
topics.reason: The proper noun is the explicit subject of the opening verb and structurally carries across the repeated accountability frame; derivational claims about the name remain subordinate to agency here.

words.gloss_range: causal preposition attaching non-accountability to the idle-oath ground
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) attaches the exemption to its cause. It makes the non-liability rest on the following idle-oath material, preventing the opening mercy from becoming a blanket release from every oath.

topics.headline: preposition marks the basis of non-liability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the exemption is tied to a specific legal ground, not to speech generally.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the following definite gerund and supplies the ground for the negated accountability clause.

words.gloss_range: idle, void, or uncounted oath material lacking intentional binding force
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّغْوِ}} ({{tr:al-laghwi}}) names oath language that never gains binding weight. Its noise-like and uncounted quality matters because the verse does not excuse all oath speech; it exempts only the material that remains void inside the oath domain, a formula also heard in the oath-law parallel (2:225).
words.root_gloss_range: idle, void, noisy, or uncounted speech; locally the oath material that lacks binding uptake

topics.headline: idle speech has no binding uptake
topics.reader_payoff: The reader distinguishes oath-noise with no legal weight from speech that has been deliberately bound.
topics.reason: The local noun is governed by the causal preposition and confined by the following oath phrase; the 2:225 formula supports the idle-oath category without changing the later contrast.

words.gloss_range: locative-domain preposition marking where idle material occurs
words.prose: {{ar:فِىٓ}} ({{tr:fī}}) locates the idle material inside oath practice. That small domain marker keeps the first clause precise: non-liability concerns what is void within oaths, not the oath institution as a whole.

topics.headline: preposition locates idleness inside oath practice
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the problem is idle material within oaths, not a cancellation of oath accountability itself.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the possessive oath noun and confines the idle material to oath practice.

words.gloss_range: your oaths, with pledged-hand and embodied commitment pressure retained beneath the local oath sense
words.prose: {{ar:أَيْمَٰنِكُمْ}} ({{tr:aymānikum}}) means your oaths here, while the root field keeps the feel of a pledged hand behind the legal noun. This first occurrence starts a fourfold chain: the same oath-domain will be bound, expiated, and finally guarded.
words.root_gloss_range: right hand, oath, pledge, power, and blessing; locally the oath-domain while retaining pledged-hand pressure

topics.headline: oaths carry pledged-hand pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears one oath object moving through exemption, binding, expiation, and guarding.
topics.reason: The local sense is oaths, while the root range supports right-hand and pledge imagery; repeated occurrences make the noun the ayah’s central legal axis.

words.gloss_range: conjunctive bridge prefixed to the adversative particle
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) carries the sentence across the boundary into contrast. It does not merely add another item; joined to the following pivot, it moves the reader from exempted idle speech toward accountable bound speech.

topics.headline: conjunction carries the turn into contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the verse move from mercy for idle speech into accountability for bound speech.
topics.reason: The conjunction is attached to the adversative pivot and carries the discourse from the exemption clause into the liability clause.

words.gloss_range: adversative particle that pivots from non-liability to liability without governing a new case ending
words.prose: {{ar:لَٰكِن}} ({{tr:lākin}}) is the ayah’s legal hinge. After the negation, it corrects any overreading of mercy: idle oath speech is not seized, but deliberately bound oath speech enters liability.
words.root_gloss_range: contrast and rectification after a prior statement; locally an adversative pivot, not a case-governing noun

topics.headline: adversative pivot from exemption to obligation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that mercy for idle oath speech is corrected against overextension by the liable case.
topics.reason: The particle introduces the affirmed accountability clause after negation and functions as a logical-legal pivot rather than as a case-governing operator.

words.gloss_range: the same Form III accountability verb now affirmed for deliberately bound oaths
words.prose: {{ar:يُؤَاخِذُكُم}} ({{tr:yuʾākhidhukum}}) repeats the accountability verb from the opening, now without the negation. The mirror matters: the divine action is the same legal holding-to-account, but the ground has changed from idle material to what was deliberately bound. The same recitational lightening can occur on this affirmative side too, preserving the legal force across the polarity pair.
words.root_gloss_range: taking, seizing, receiving, adopting, and holding to account; the local Form III use selects legal accountability while retaining seizure pressure

topics.headline: same verb returns under affirmation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that liability depends on the ground of speech, not on a new verb or new authority.
topics.reason: The repeated verb mirrors the opening one while reversing polarity, so the contrast lies in the complement that grounds accountability.

words.gloss_range: causal preposition introducing the accountable basis
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) introduces the cause of liability. It ties the second account-taking to the following bound matter, so the verse distinguishes mere oath wording from an accountable act of making it firm.

topics.headline: preposition grounds liability in what was bound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that liability is attached to deliberate binding, not to oath wording by itself.
topics.reason: The preposition with the following relative phrase marks the ground on which the second accountability verb applies.

words.gloss_range: relative or verbal-noun-like marker introducing the bound oath content or binding act
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) lets the accountable ground be heard as the bound matter and, by extension, the act of binding it. The ambiguity is useful but local: it does not create a new object outside the following oath-binding clause.

topics.headline: relative marker leaves object and act in view
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees liability attached both to what was contracted and to the act of contracting it.
topics.reason: The local grammar supports a relative complement and CRITICAL rows note a verbal-noun reading; both remain bounded by the following finite verb and oath object.

words.gloss_range: you deliberately bound or made firm the oaths; variant readings broaden the binding profile without undoing the local agency
words.prose: {{ar:عَقَّدتُّمُ}} ({{tr:ʿaqqadtumu}}) is where loose speech becomes a knot. The Form II perfect places the binding act on the addressed oath-makers, and the object is the oaths themselves. Variant readings can let the binding sound simple, intensive, mutual, or can push the oath itself forward as grammatical actor, but all keep the legal point: this is not accidental oath-noise.
words.root_gloss_range: tying, knotting, contracting, and making firm; locally deliberate oath-binding that creates liability

topics.headline: intensive binding turns oath speech into liability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels casual speech tighten into a legal knot made by the oath-makers themselves.
topics.reason: The Form II perfect with second-person plural subject and explicit oath object selects deliberate binding; variant readings add intensity, simple tying, or mutual contracting as apparatus rather than replacing the local parse.

words.gloss_range: the oaths as direct object of binding, with variant prominence for the oath entity kept as apparatus
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَيْمَٰنَ}} ({{tr:al-aymāna}}) names the oaths as the thing bound in the main reading. This second occurrence reuses the opening oath-domain but changes its legal state: it is no longer idle material inside oaths, but the object made firm by deliberate action.
words.root_gloss_range: right hand, oath, pledge, power, and blessing; locally the oath-domain while retaining pledged-hand pressure

topics.headline: oaths become the object acted on
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same oath-domain now shifted from exempted space to a legally acted-on object.
topics.reason: The main reading makes the noun accusative object of the binding verb; the nominative variant can sharpen oath prominence without controlling the canonical parse.

words.gloss_range: resultative or explanatory connector introducing the expiation consequence
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) opens the consequence. The expiation list that follows is not a new devotional topic; it is the structured result of deliberately binding an oath.

topics.headline: result particle opens the consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the expiation list as the consequence of deliberate binding, not as detached advice.
topics.reason: The particle follows the liability clause and opens the nominal expiation statement.

words.gloss_range: its expiation or covering-repair, with the suffix tying the remedy back to the bound-oath liability
words.prose: {{ar:كَفَّٰرَتُهُۥٓ}} ({{tr:kaffāratuhu}}) names the repair as a covering, and its suffix fastens that covering to the oath breach just stated. The same root can describe denial as covering truth, but here the covering is lawful expiation: a breach is covered so the community can move toward gratitude. The same repair noun belongs to a legal-expiation cluster inside the surah (5:45; 5:95) and to wider tiered expiation passages (4:92; 58:3-4), with this occurrence marking the oath-specific instance.
words.root_gloss_range: covering, concealing, denial, and expiatory covering; locally lawful covering or repair for oath breach

topics.headline: expiation covers the oath breach
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees repair as a lawful covering tied to this breach, not as generic charity.
topics.reason: The noun is a specialized legal term from the covering root, and the suffix points back to the oath liability; broader denial meanings remain contrastive rather than local sense.

words.gloss_range: causative feeding as the first concrete expiation option, specified by recipients and household benchmark
words.prose: {{ar:إِطْعَامُ}} ({{tr:iṭʿāmu}}) turns eating into making others eat. The first remedy sends sustenance outward to a counted vulnerable group, and the later household benchmark keeps it concrete rather than symbolic.
words.root_gloss_range: tasting, eating, food, and causing another to eat; locally causative feeding as remedy or benchmark

topics.headline: first remedy makes others eat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the first option as concrete outward sustenance, not a symbolic payment.
topics.reason: The Form IV gerund names causing others to eat, and the following count, recipient group, and household standard specify the act.

words.gloss_range: ten as a bounded count of recipients, with social-group pressure but no independent legal class
words.prose: {{ar:عَشَرَةِ}} ({{tr:ʿasharati}}) fixes the feeding remedy at ten recipients. Its social-field pressure lets the number feel like a small visible group, while the grammar keeps it a concrete count rather than a vague communal symbol.
words.root_gloss_range: ten, grouping, and social association; locally a counted set of ten recipients

topics.headline: ten forms a visible recipient group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the repair is socially distributed across a concrete group rather than kept inward.
topics.reason: The numeral governs the following needy recipients in construct; social intimacy pressure can enrich the count but does not replace its numerical function.

words.gloss_range: needy persons marked by vulnerability and immobilized need, serving as recipients of feeding and clothing
words.prose: {{ar:مَسَٰكِينَ}} ({{tr:masākīna}}) identifies the ten recipients as people held down by need. The stillness pressure in the root makes feeding them feel like relief for immobilized vulnerability, and the later clothing suffix keeps this same group in view. The separate listing of poverty categories (9:60) keeps this recipient class from collapsing into generic poverty, while the same surah’s compensation frame (5:95) keeps feeding vulnerable persons in the legal-remedy field.
words.root_gloss_range: stillness, dwelling, rest, and immobilized need; locally vulnerable needy recipients

topics.headline: needy recipients are socially immobilized
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the beneficiaries as people constrained by need, and the same group remains in view for clothing.
topics.reason: The intensive plural supplies the counted recipient group; lexical stillness pressure survives, while comparisons with other poverty terms remain contrastive.

words.gloss_range: qualitative or partitive preposition introducing the standard from which feeding is measured
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) draws the measure from a standard rather than leaving it undefined. It points the feeding obligation toward the quality-range of ordinary household provision.

topics.headline: preposition draws the measure from household practice
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the amount is calibrated from a real domestic standard.
topics.reason: The preposition before the comparative adjective draws the feeding measure from the household feeding range.

words.gloss_range: middle, balanced, or best-measured portion of what the household is fed
words.prose: {{ar:أَوْسَطِ}} ({{tr:awsaṭi}}) sets the feeding measure at the middle, balanced, or best-measured level of ordinary household food. The word resists both extravagance and evasion, and its wider centrality echoes, including the middle community (2:143) and middle prayer (2:238), make fairness part of the legal texture. A variant sound profile confirms measured balance rather than introducing a different legal object.
words.root_gloss_range: middle, balanced, central, and best-measured; locally the fair household feeding standard

topics.headline: middle standard resists excess and evasion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the feeding measure as fair balance drawn from household practice, not a token minimum.
topics.reason: The comparative form and local construction support a measured household standard; wider centrality echoes such as the middle community (2:143) and middle prayer (2:238) enrich without replacing the legal benchmark.

words.gloss_range: relative marker linking the standard to what is actually fed
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) links the standard to what is actually fed. The measure is not abstract market value; it is drawn from lived domestic practice.

topics.headline: relative marker ties measure to actual feeding
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the law uses lived household practice as its measuring point.
topics.reason: The relative marker introduces the household feeding clause that supplies the benchmark.

words.gloss_range: you habitually cause to eat; recurring household provision used as the expiation benchmark
words.prose: {{ar:تُطْعِمُونَ}} ({{tr:tuṭʿimūna}}) makes the benchmark habitual: what you keep causing your household to eat. The same food root links the remedy to ordinary provision, so received sustenance becomes a measure for repair. The prior command to eat from provision (5:88) is ethically reversed here into the standard for feeding others.
words.root_gloss_range: tasting, eating, food, and causing another to eat; locally causative feeding as remedy or benchmark

topics.headline: habitual feeding supplies the benchmark
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the community measured by its recurring provision for its own dependents.
topics.reason: The imperfect Form IV verb is second-person plural and repeats the feeding root as an ongoing household practice.

words.gloss_range: your household or people under your care as the baseline for feeding quality
words.prose: {{ar:أَهْلِيكُمْ}} ({{tr:ahlīkum}}) supplies the concrete care-unit used as the standard. The law does not ask for an undefined charitable amount; it measures the poor against what the oath-maker normally provides for those under household responsibility. Variant expansion of the family-people field broadens the heard belonging-unit without changing the obligation, and the addressed community carried from provision (5:88) remains the liable and repairing community here.
words.root_gloss_range: family, household, inhabitants, or those belonging to a class; locally the household baseline of provision

topics.headline: household belonging sets the standard
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees expiation calibrated by the giver’s own care-unit rather than by an abstract minimum.
topics.reason: The noun functions as object of the feeding verb with a possessive suffix, anchoring the standard in the addressees’ domestic belonging-unit.

words.gloss_range: disjunctive choice marker between material expiation options
words.prose: {{ar:أَوْ}} ({{tr:aw}}) opens choice within the expiation set. Feeding and clothing are coordinated alternatives, not stages that must both happen in sequence.

topics.headline: first choice marker opens alternatives
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears feeding and clothing as legal alternatives inside one remedy set.
topics.reason: The particle coordinates feeding with clothing as alternatives rather than chronological steps.

words.gloss_range: their clothing or clothing them, a concrete covering option directed to the needy recipients
words.prose: {{ar:كِسْوَتُهُمْ}} ({{tr:kiswatuhum}}) makes the second remedy bodily covering. The suffix keeps the needy recipients in view, so clothing is not abstract value; it is material care parallel to feeding, with a covering logic that resonates with the larger expiation field. Honored-covering resonance remains background, and the maintenance vocabulary in nursing law (2:233) keeps clothing within concrete support duties.
words.root_gloss_range: covering with clothing and concrete bodily covering; locally clothing the same needy recipients

topics.headline: clothing covers the same recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the second option as bodily covering for the same needy group, parallel to feeding as material care.
topics.reason: The noun is coordinated with feeding and carries the plural suffix back to the recipients; variant readings sharpen object-versus-standard questions without detaching the option from bodily covering.

words.gloss_range: disjunctive choice marker before the freeing option
words.prose: {{ar:أَوْ}} ({{tr:aw}}) adds the third option to the coordinated set. The list moves from feeding to clothing to freeing while remaining one structured remedy.

topics.headline: second choice marker completes the triad
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears freeing added as a third coordinated option, not an unrelated afterthought.
topics.reason: The particle coordinates the third material option with feeding and clothing inside one expiation set.

words.gloss_range: freeing or manumission as a required expiation act, locally unqualified by the faith adjective found in 4:92
words.prose: {{ar:تَحْرِيرُ}} ({{tr:taḥrīru}}) names liberation as an act to be performed. It governs the following neck, making the remedy social release from bondage. The broader root pressure of freeing from obstruction remains image-pressure, while the local object selects social manumission; the parallel phrase in accidental-killing law adds a faith qualifier (4:92), while this oath setting does not.
words.root_gloss_range: freedom, release, heat, and making a thing clear or free; locally manumission as an expiation act

topics.headline: freeing is an act of release
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the third option as releasing a constrained person, with the local wording not adding the faith qualifier found elsewhere.
topics.reason: The gerund names the act of freeing and governs the neck noun; the 4:92 parallel supports the fixed phrase while showing that the local oath setting lacks the added faith qualifier.

words.gloss_range: a neck as bodily synecdoche for an enslaved person under restraint and oversight
words.prose: {{ar:رَقَبَةٍۢ}} ({{tr:raqabatin}}) gives liberation a bodily focus. The neck stands for the constrained person, the vulnerable site of yoke, collar, and oversight, so freeing a neck means undoing embodied control. The watcher and watched tension also recalls watcher language (4:1), but here the local phrase selects the watched-over body released from restraint.
words.root_gloss_range: neck, watching, oversight, and being under control; locally the neck as bodily synecdoche for an enslaved person

topics.headline: neck names the constrained person
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the freed person through the vulnerable bodily site where restraint is felt.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by the freeing gerund and its root field supports neck, watching, and control; the local sense is the person represented through the neck.

words.gloss_range: conditional-result connector opening the fallback branch
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) turns from the material options to the fallback branch. The law anticipates inability inside its own structure, so lack of means does not dissolve the remedy.

topics.headline: result marker introduces inability fallback
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees inability anticipated inside the law rather than treated as an afterthought.
topics.reason: The particle precedes the conditional pronoun and shifts from the option triad to the inability condition.

words.gloss_range: conditional pronoun applying the fallback to whoever cannot meet the material options
words.prose: {{ar:مَن}} ({{tr:man}}) universalizes the fallback. It does not name a fixed class; it opens the fasting substitute to whoever cannot find the means for the material remedies.

topics.headline: whoever universalizes the fallback
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the fallback applies to any oath-maker who lacks means.
topics.reason: The pronoun functions as the subject of the conditional clause before the negated finding verb.

words.gloss_range: jussive negator before the finding verb
words.prose: {{ar:لَّمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) negates the finding verb in the condition. The fallback is triggered by not finding the needed means, not by simply preferring the easier path.

topics.headline: jussive negation triggers fallback
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the substitute triggered by actual non-availability, not preference.
topics.reason: The particle negates the following jussive verb inside the conditional clause.

words.gloss_range: find, possess, or have access to the means; here negated as practical inability across material options
words.prose: {{ar:يَجِدْ}} ({{tr:yajid}}) leaves the missing object unstated because the prior options supply it. The condition means not finding or having access to the means for feeding, clothing, or freeing, and the negated jussive makes that lack settled rather than speculative. It is a legal fallback formula also used in expiation settings such as accidental killing (4:92), pilgrimage compensation (2:196), and formal separation repair (58:4).
words.root_gloss_range: finding, having access, practical possession, and inward experience; locally inability to find or possess material means

topics.headline: not finding means practical inability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees inability as lack of practical access to the material remedies.
topics.reason: The object is omitted and recovered from the preceding material options; lexical range supports access or possession, while the legal formula confines it to remedy capacity.

words.gloss_range: apodosis marker introducing the fasting response
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) introduces the response to inability. Fasting now appears as the legal answer after non-finding, not as a fourth material option beside feeding, clothing, and freeing.

topics.headline: result marker introduces fasting substitute
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears fasting as the answer to inability, not a fourth equal material option.
topics.reason: The particle follows the inability condition and opens the nominal fasting phrase.

words.gloss_range: fasting or disciplined abstention as the accessible fallback expiation
words.prose: {{ar:صِيَامُ}} ({{tr:ṣiyāmu}}) shifts the remedy inward. When provision cannot be redirected outward through feeding, clothing, or freeing, the body itself bears disciplined restraint, making the fallback accessible without material resources. The provision frame from the prior ayah (5:88) turns from receiving food to withholding from food, and the same three-day phrase appears as a compensation formula in the pilgrimage setting (2:196).
words.root_gloss_range: abstention, withholding, cessation, and fasting; locally bodily restraint as fallback expiation

topics.headline: fasting turns repair inward when means are absent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the remedy shift from outward provision to bodily restraint when material resources are unavailable.
topics.reason: The gerund names the substitute after the non-finding condition; cross-passage formula evidence supports three-day fasting as a compensation pattern.

words.gloss_range: three as the fixed count governing the fasting days, with consecutiveness raised by variant evidence
words.prose: {{ar:ثَلَٰثَةِ}} ({{tr:thalāthati}}) bounds the fasting substitute. It fixes the remedy at three days; variant evidence can raise whether those days are consecutive, but the local count itself remains concrete and finite. The same duration in pilgrimage compensation (2:196) makes the number a portable minimal fasting measure rather than an isolated count.
words.root_gloss_range: three, thirds, and being third; locally a bounded three-day measure

topics.headline: three gives the fallback a finite measure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the substitute is concrete and bounded rather than open-ended penitence.
topics.reason: The numeral governs the following days; variant-reading evidence can raise consecutiveness as a legal question without changing the canonical count.

words.gloss_range: days as the legal unit of fasting duration; broader period senses remain background only
words.prose: {{ar:أَيَّامٍۢ}} ({{tr:ayyāmin}}) supplies the unit of the substitute. The broader root can mark bounded time, but the legal construction selects lived days, turning the fallback from material value into embodied duration. The indefinite ending also cadences the shift from freeing a neck to counting days.
words.root_gloss_range: day or bounded period; locally ordinary lived days as the legal unit

topics.headline: days make the substitute embodied time
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the fasting fallback measured in lived time rather than commodity value.
topics.reason: The noun is the counted unit after three, so ordinary days are selected while broader bounded-time senses are not the local meaning.

words.gloss_range: summarizing demonstrative pointing back to the entire option-and-fallback structure
words.prose: {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}) points back over the whole structure just laid out. It gathers feeding, clothing, freeing, and the fasting fallback before the sentence names that gathered system as oath expiation.
words.root_gloss_range: deictic pointing and summary; locally gathers the preceding legal structure or points back to it

topics.headline: demonstrative gathers the whole remedy structure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees feeding, clothing, freeing, and fasting gathered into one named system.
topics.reason: The demonstrative functions as subject of the following identification and points back to the preceding legal sequence.

words.gloss_range: expiation in construct, identifying the gathered option set as the covering-repair for oaths
words.prose: {{ar:كَفَّٰرَةُ}} ({{tr:kaffāratu}}) seals the gathered options into one legal category. By repeating the covering-repair noun after the list, the verse brackets feeding, clothing, freeing, and fasting as one expiatory unit.
words.root_gloss_range: covering, concealing, denial, and expiatory covering; locally lawful covering or repair for oath breach

topics.headline: predicate seals the option set as expiation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the whole sequence sealed as one legal covering for oath breach.
topics.reason: The noun predicates what the demonstrative has gathered and repeats the expiation term after the option list.

words.gloss_range: your oaths as the construct complement limiting the summarized expiation
words.prose: {{ar:أَيْمَٰنِكُمْ}} ({{tr:aymānikum}}) makes the summary oath-specific. The construct prevents the option set from floating into generic charity and ties the remedy back to the oath-domain introduced at the opening.
words.root_gloss_range: right hand, oath, pledge, power, and blessing; locally the oath-domain while retaining pledged-hand pressure

topics.headline: construct limits the expiation to your oaths
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the remedy tied back to the oath-domain instead of generalized into charity law.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive under the expiation construct and repeats the oath-domain after the remedy is explained.

words.gloss_range: temporal-conditional marker introducing the oath-taking trigger
words.prose: {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) introduces the circumstance that activates the summary. The expiation belongs to oath-taking, not to a standing charity rule detached from sworn speech.

topics.headline: temporal condition names when the summary applies
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the remedy is activated by oath-taking, not by standing charity need alone.
topics.reason: The adverb introduces the following completed oath act as the circumstance for the summarized expiation.

words.gloss_range: you have sworn; completed oath-taking act distinct from the oath-object vocabulary
words.prose: {{ar:حَلَفْتُمْ}} ({{tr:ḥalaftum}}) names the completed act of swearing with a different root from the repeated oath noun. That distinction matters: the verse separates performing the oath from preserving the oath-object that now must be guarded. The simple perfect marks an actual completed oath, not the habitual or intensive false-swearing profile known elsewhere.
words.root_gloss_range: swearing and oath-taking; locally the completed oath act that triggers the summary

topics.headline: different root names the act of swearing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader distinguishes the act of swearing from the oath object that must later be guarded.
topics.reason: The perfect Form I verb names the performed act, and the nearby oath-object noun supplies a second root for the product of swearing.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction linking the legal exposition to the guarding command
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins the legal exposition to the direct command. After the remedy has been explained, the discourse turns the audience toward prevention.

topics.headline: conjunction joins remedy to command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears prevention follow remedy as the next practical step.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the direct imperative after the summarized expiation clause.

words.gloss_range: guard, preserve, keep, observe, and avoid neglecting oath practice; locally a second-person plural imperative after the remedy
words.prose: {{ar:ٱحْفَظُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:iḥfaẓū}}) shifts from explanation to command. Guarding here can include keeping valid oaths and protecting speech from careless oath-making; it turns knowledge of expiation into preventive discipline, with a guard-and-middle echo to the prayer passage (2:238).
words.root_gloss_range: guarding, preserving, remembering, observing, and not neglecting; locally protecting oath practice after remedy is known

topics.headline: guarding means preserving and restraining oath practice
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a command that includes both keeping valid oaths and avoiding careless oath-making.
topics.reason: The imperative form addresses the community directly after legal exposition; the root range supports both keeping and guarding against misuse, while echoes with guarding and middle language (2:238) remain intertextual support.

words.gloss_range: your oaths as the direct object of the guarding imperative
words.prose: {{ar:أَيْمَٰنَكُمْ}} ({{tr:aymānakum}}) is now the object of the guarding command. The noun that began inside exemption and moved through binding and expiation ends as an entrusted object requiring preservation.
words.root_gloss_range: right hand, oath, pledge, power, and blessing; locally the oath-domain while retaining pledged-hand pressure

topics.headline: oaths become entrusted objects
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the repeated oath-domain end under direct responsibility.
topics.reason: The noun is accusative object of the command and is the fourth occurrence of the oath-domain in the ayah.

words.gloss_range: comparative preposition prefixed to the following demonstrative
words.prose: {{ar:كَ}} ({{tr:ka}}) begins the comparison frame. It makes the just-explained oath ruling the model for how divine clarification works.

topics.headline: comparative particle starts the clarification frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the just-explained law offered as a model of divine clarification.
topics.reason: The particle combines with the demonstrative to frame the preceding exposition as the manner of clarification.

words.gloss_range: demonstrative object of the comparative particle pointing back to the rule as a whole
words.prose: {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}) points back to the whole legal exposition as the way clarification happens. The phrase belongs to a recurring explanatory closure also found in legal or guidance contexts such as fasting (2:187), wine and gambling (2:219), divorce (2:242), charity imagery (2:266), communal holding (3:103), and household-entry rules (24:58; 24:61).
words.root_gloss_range: deictic pointing and summary; locally gathers the preceding legal structure or points back to it

topics.headline: demonstrative points back to the legal exposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the whole rule recast as exemplary clarification, not mere procedure.
topics.reason: The demonstrative in the comparative phrase points back to the preceding legal exposition; recurring formula evidence supports the closure frame.

words.gloss_range: Form II making clear or making distinct, with God as subject, the community as beneficiary, and signs as object
words.prose: {{ar:يُبَيِّنُ}} ({{tr:yubayyinu}}) presents clarification as active making-distinct. The verb gathers the ayah’s separations: idle oath material, bound oath, material remedies, inability fallback, and prevention are all sorted as divine guidance, not just legal data. The following purpose clause aims that clarification toward gratitude, so the legal sorting is meant to transform response rather than merely transfer information.
words.root_gloss_range: separation, distinction, clarity, declaration, and proof; locally God making legal cases distinct

topics.headline: divine clarification separates legal cases
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees legal detail itself as the act of making signs distinct for the community.
topics.reason: The Form II imperfect selects active clarification; root separation pressure survives as the verse distinguishes idle oath, bound oath, material remedies, inability fallback, and prevention.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name as explicit agent of the closing clarification verb
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:allāhu}}) returns as the named agent of clarification after being the agent of accountability. The same divine source judges oath speech and explains its remedy. From the prior ayah’s provision and reverence frame (5:88), the divine role expands into pardon, judgment, and clarification over verbal obligation.
words.root_gloss_range: divinity, worship, refuge, and awe; here the proper name functions as the named divine agent of accountability and clarification

topics.headline: divine agent returns at clarification close
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same divine source judge oath speech and explain its remedy.
topics.reason: The name is the nominative subject of the clarification verb and echoes the divine agency at the accountability opening.

words.gloss_range: for you; benefactive-dative phrase marking the addressed community as recipient of clarification
words.prose: {{ar:لَكُمْ}} ({{tr:lakum}}) places the addressed community in the beneficiary position. Before the signs are named, the grammar foregrounds that the clarification is for their practical guidance.

topics.headline: benefactive phrase foregrounds the addressed community
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees clarification directed for the community’s practical benefit before the signs are named.
topics.reason: The compound prepositional phrase precedes the direct object and marks the second-person plural community as beneficiary.

words.gloss_range: His signs or revealed markers; local sense is clarified divine signs, while root-dispute claims remain subordinate
words.prose: {{ar:ءَايَٰتِهِۦ}} ({{tr:āyātihi}}) is what God clarifies: His signs. The practical oath rule is therefore framed as revelatory guidance, not mere regulation, while disputed root analysis stays secondary to the clear local role of signs being made plain.
words.root_gloss_range: sign, mark, verse, or indicator, with disputed root analysis; locally revealed signs clarified by the ruling

topics.headline: legal detail is framed as divine signs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the oath-expiation rule as revelatory guidance rather than mere regulation.
topics.reason: The noun is the direct object of the clarification verb with divine possessive suffix; CRITICAL root-dispute rows require caution around derivation while preserving sign/verse semantics.

words.gloss_range: so that perhaps you may; purposive hope or intended outcome from the addressee side
words.prose: {{ar:لَعَلَّكُمْ}} ({{tr:laʿallakum}}) opens the outcome clause. The legal explanation does not close with penalty alone; it aims the addressed community toward the response made possible by clarified mercy.

topics.headline: purpose particle opens gratitude outcome
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the legal exposition close with intended response, not penalty alone.
topics.reason: The particle opens the final purpose clause and does not imply divine uncertainty; it orients clarification toward the community’s response.

words.gloss_range: you give thanks or keep acknowledging benefit; ongoing grateful response to clarified oath remedy
words.prose: {{ar:تَشْكُرُونَ}} ({{tr:tashkurūna}}) leaves gratitude as an ongoing response. After the fault is covered through expiation, the closing word moves the community toward open acknowledgment of divine clarification; the contrast with the covering root is especially strong because the ayah has twice named expiation as covering-repair. Compared with the fasting-law close aimed at mindfulness (2:187), this oath-law clarification specifically seeks gratitude for mercy and remedy.
words.root_gloss_range: gratitude, acknowledgment of benefit, and visible thriving; locally ongoing grateful response to clarified remedy

topics.headline: gratitude answers clarified covering-repair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah move from covering an oath fault to openly acknowledging divine guidance.
topics.reason: The imperfect verb makes gratitude ongoing; root contrast with covering-repair is valid as an interpretive arc, while concrete thriving imagery remains image-pressure rather than the selected local sense.
